items.text: cli-core's HTTPClient has no ExtraHeaders mechanism. requestV1() delegates to APIClient.Request() → HTTPClient.Do() which only sets Authorization and X-Dry-Run headers. The identity header cannot be injected through the existing chain without either (a) extending cli-core's HTTPClient, or (b) wrapping the http.Client's Transport with a RoundTripper.

items.context: requestV1() calls a.core.APIClient.Request() which goes through HTTPClient.DoWithContext(). This chain has no hook for extra headers. requestMultipartV1() builds requests manually and already iterates AuthHeaders(). We need a way to inject X-Agent-Identity-Token without modifying the out-of-scope packages/cli-core.

options.label: Custom http.RoundTripper that wraps DefaultTransport and injects the header
options.rationale: Go-idiomatic pattern. Set it on the http.Client before APIClient uses it. No cli-core changes needed. All requests through that client automatically get the header. Clean separation of concerns. Recommended because it works transparently for both requestV1 and requestMultipartV1.

options.label: Add ExtraHeaders map to cli-core's HTTPClient
options.rationale: Cleaner API surface — HTTPClient gains a SetExtraHeaders() method like SetToken(). But requires modifying packages/cli-core, which the scope says is out of bounds. Would benefit other scenarios adopting identity later.

options.label: Replace requestV1() with manual request construction (like requestMultipartV1)
options.rationale: No new abstractions, just duplicate the manual request pattern. But duplicates ~30 lines of HTTPClient.DoWithContext logic and creates drift risk if cli-core changes its request handling.

items.topic: Middleware testing strategy for agent-manager verification
items.context: The identity middleware calls cliutil.VerifyIdentity() which makes an HTTP request to agent-manager. Tests need to avoid depending on a running agent-manager. The existing test patterns in swarm-manager use httptest.NewServer for handler tests but there are no middleware-specific test patterns.

options.label: Interface-based: define a Verifier interface, inject real or mock implementation
options.rationale: Standard Go testability pattern. Middleware takes a Verifier interface; production uses cliutil-backed implementation, tests use a stub. Clear, explicit, no global state. Recommended because it's the cleanest testing seam and matches the testutil patterns already in use.

options.label: httptest.NewServer as fake agent-manager in tests
options.rationale: Integration-style: spin up a fake HTTP server that responds to /api/v1/identity/verify. Tests exercise the real HTTP path. More realistic but slower, more boilerplate, and tests are coupled to agent-manager's API shape.

items.context: The plan says created_by is set at creation time and immutable. SaveItem() does a read-modify-write: it reads existing spec.json, merges known fields from the BacklogItem struct, and preserves unknown fields. We need to decide where to enforce immutability so that updates cannot overwrite created_by.

options.label: Store-level: SaveItem() reads existing created_by before write and preserves it if already set
options.rationale: Defense in depth — no matter what handler passes, the store ensures created_by can never change once written. Fits naturally into the existing read-modify-write pattern. Recommended because it makes the invariant impossible to violate regardless of caller.

options.label: Handler-level only: create handler sets it, update handler omits it from the struct
options.rationale: Simpler — relies on convention that update handlers don't populate CreatedBy. But a bug in any handler could silently overwrite provenance. No safety net.

items.topic: Provenance propagation to agent activity records
items.context: Agent activity records currently get RequestedBy from hardcoded strings in handlers (e.g., 'swarm-manager', 'swarm-manager-ui'). With the identity middleware, provenance is available in context. We need to decide how activity records should adopt provenance.

options.label: Middleware sets provenance in context; activity Spec reads from context when RequestedBy is empty
options.rationale: Minimal handler changes — existing code that sets RequestedBy explicitly keeps working, but CLI-initiated requests get automatic agent provenance from context. The activity Spec.normalized() method already has a default fallback. Recommended because it's backward-compatible and low-touch.

options.label: Each handler explicitly reads provenance from context and sets RequestedBy
options.rationale: More explicit — every handler consciously decides what to set. But requires touching every handler that creates activities, and risks missed handlers.

plan_updates: Refined Phase 1 with specific implementation detail about the header injection gap (HTTPClient lacks ExtraHeaders). Added testing strategy detail to Phase 6. Refined Phase 3 with store-level immutability approach. Added agent activity propagation detail to Phase 4.
